name: application-product-card
title: Product Card
description: E-commerce product card with a hover quick-view overlay, title, star rating, price with an optional compare-at price, and an add-to-cart action.
useWhen: Building a product listing or catalog grid where each item needs an image, price, and quick add-to-cart action.
You want to surface a discount by showing both the sale price and the original compare-at price.
A hover quick-view affordance would let users preview a product without a full page navigation.
avoidWhen: The item has no price or purchase action — the generic `card` component is a better fit for editorial or content tiles.
You're showing an item already in the cart with quantity controls — use `cart-line-item` for that row-based, already-added state instead.
Hover states aren't reachable on the target device (e.g. a touch-primary storefront) — ensure quick-view has a non-hover fallback such as a persistent affordance.
responsiveBehavior: Fixed-aspect square image scales with the card's width; the card itself is meant to sit inside a responsive grid that controls column count per breakpoint.
accessibility: The star rating is a single role="img" group with an aria-label stating the numeric rating and review count, rather than 5 separate ambiguous icons.
The add-to-cart button is icon-only with an aria-label naming the specific product, not a generic "Add to cart".
The discount badge and compare-at price communicate the sale through visible text (strikethrough + label), not color alone.
The product image's alt text describes the product, not the marketing copy already present in the title.

variants.title: Product Card
variants.description: Headphones product card with a discount badge, hover quick-view, 4.5-star rating, and add-to-cart.
accessibility: Quick-view only appears on hover/focus of the card group, so it must also be reachable via keyboard focus, not pointer hover alone.

variants.title: Product Card (Dark)
variants.description: Product card adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Text and star colors are tuned to meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark surface.
